Order
This miscellaneous appeal by appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

1988 is arising out of the Award dated 19.01.2022 passed by 1st Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manawar District Dhar (hereinafter it would be referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.140/2017 seeking enhancement of compensation amount.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manawar District Dhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, for the death of Yashwant (husband of appellant No.1- herein), the Claims Tribunal after assessing the income of deceased at Rs.6000/- per month, (age of deceased 30 years) applying 40% towards future prospects and applying multiplier of 17 including filial NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6100 2 MA-3734-2022 consortium, funeral and loss of estate, has awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,71,000/- along-with interest in favour of Claimants from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower side.

The Claims Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income Pinky vs Mukesh on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43010585/
1 of the deceased as Rs.6000/- per month.
As per the evidence came on record, he was a shoopkeeper by profession.

However, accepting earning of deceased as Rs.7150/- per month in view of the Minimum Wages Act and adding future prospects, applying adequate multiplier including compensation under other conventional heads, the reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned Award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case, which does not call for any interference by this Court.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellants.

So far as income of the deceased is concerned, as per the evidence that came on record, he was a shopkeeper, therefore, in view of Minimum Wages Act, his income should be assessed appropriately after looking to his involment of the works and numbers of dependency therefore, the income of the deceased should be Rs.7125/-
per month +application of 40% of the monthly income i.e. NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6100 3 MA-3734-2022 7125x40/100=2850/- per month.
Therefore, his income is fixed as Rs.7,125 per month instead of Rs.6000/- per month as assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

8. It is needless to mention here that appellant No.1 is the wife, appellant No.2 is son of deceased and appellants No.3 and 4 are parents and appellant nos.5 and 6 are the sister and son of the deceased respectively, Therefore, they are entitled to get towards loss of filial consortium @
Rs.44,000/- each.

9. In view of above, the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is modified as under:
 HEAD AMOUN

Monthly income Rs.7125/-
Future prospects 40 % i.e. Rs.7125x40/100= Rs.2850/- After deduction of Loss of dependency 1/4th i.e.Rs.9975-(25%)2493.75=7481.25 Yearly Dependency =7481.25x12=89775/-

Multiplier 17=Rs.89,775x17=15,26,175/-
Total amount towards dependency: 15,26,175/-
Other Heads:-
Loss of filial Consortium-(Rs.44,000X 6) =Rs. 2,64,000/-
Funeral expenses = Rs. 16,5  Loss of Estate = Rs. 16,5 Pinky vs Mukesh on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43010585/
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.18,23,175/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.11,71,000/-.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6100 4 MA-3734-2022

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant are entitled to an additional sum of (Rs.18,23,175-11,71,000) = Rs.6,52,175/-
over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
11. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The claimants are entitled to get total amount of compensation i.e. Rs.11,71,000/- + Rs.6,52,175/- =18,23,175/-.

The enhanced amount i.e.
Rs. 6,52,175/- shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three month s from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
13. In view of above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants- claimants stands disposed of.
(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE amit Pinky vs Mukesh on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43010585/
